sector: Material handling equipment and aerial work platform rental

company_pe.source: RHP pp. 104-106 (Basis for Issue Price); PAT p. 223
company_pe.note: EPS is on 1,00,10,000 weighted shares (post the 1,000:1 bonus of Sep-2024). It excludes the 14,28,500 shares allotted on 27-Jul-2026 on conversion of director loans, so on the 1,14,38,500 pre-issue shares FY26 EPS is Rs 25.49 (P/E 9.10x-9.61x across the band), and on the 1,63,40,500 post-issue shares Rs 17.85 (P/E 13.0x-13.7x). Weighted average EPS FY24-26 Rs 25.71. The industry P/E is the RHP's two peers only (Seemax Resources 16.07x, Leap India 76.81x).

business_stage: Scaling (capital-intensive fleet growth; issue funds new fleet)

anchor.source: Anchor portion, if any, bid on 18-Nov-2026; allocation not reachable

call_basis: Call rule (ROUTINE.md hard rule 6), judged at the Rs 245 upper band: the Neutral value of Rs 219 is 10.4% below the price, inside the 10-30% band, and the Bull value of Rs 262 is above it, so the call is Neutral. At the Rs 232 floor the Neutral value is 5.4% below, which would read Subscribe. No material issue was found in the RHP.
reference_note: Upper band Rs 245 (49,02,000 fresh shares, Rs 120.10 cr). At Rs 245: market cap Rs 400.3 cr post-issue; P/E 13.7x on FY26 PAT on post-issue shares (9.6x on pre-issue shares; 8.4x on the company's EPS of Rs 29.13, which excludes the Jul-2026 loan-conversion shares); P/B about 1.75x post-issue; EV/EBITDA about 6.4x. RHP peer Seemax Resources 16.1x. Objects floor Rs 222.
headline: An equipment-rental company (2,646 owned forklifts and reach trucks, 33 aerial work platforms, 357 customers) with FY26 revenue of Rs 211 cr, a 31% EBITDA margin and Rs 29 cr PAT, raising Rs 120 cr of fresh money mostly for new fleet at 13.7x FY26 earnings post-issue; fair value Rs 219 (Neutral) because fleet growth uses all the cash it generates.
red_flags: Revenue from operations Rs 130.12 cr (FY24) -> Rs 179.48 cr -> Rs 211.36 cr (FY26); PAT Rs 18.05 -> 24.43 -> 29.16 cr; EBITDA margin 30.76% (pp. 107, 223)
Cumulative CFO Rs 115.10 cr vs PAT Rs 71.64 cr over FY24-26, but fleet capex of Rs 188.29 cr was largely debt-funded: borrowings Rs 164.08 cr vs net worth Rs 85.55 cr at Mar-26 (p. 224)
Rs 35.00 cr of interest-free promoter loans converted into equity at Rs 245 on 27-Jul-2026, cutting debt to about Rs 129 cr before the issue (p. 76)

Promoter-group dealings disclosed: Rs 25.21 cr of fleet bought from Watrana Traction Company in FY26; hire charges and battery purchases from group entities; same-line group company under a non-compete (pp. 61-62, 213)
FY26 trading margin on machinery and battery sales rose to Rs 10.15 cr from Rs 3.94 cr, about the whole of the FY26 PBT increase (p. 237)
Fair value Rs 179 / 219 / 262 vs Rs 245; top customer 3.33% and top ten 25.70% of revenue (p. 163)

strengths: Revenue up 62% in two years; PAT Rs 29.16 cr (p. 223)
Spread customer base: top ten 25.70% of revenue, 357 customers (p. 163)
weaknesses: Fleet growth debt-funded; borrowings 1.92x net worth at Mar-26 (p. 222)
Free cash flow negative after fleet capex
Labour-heavy model: employee cost 43% of revenue, 3,883 staff (pp. 157, 223)
opportunities: Indian MHE rental market USD 2.33 bn in 2026, 13% CAGR to 2036 per the company-commissioned Infomerics report (p. 134)
AWP rental (33 units) as a second line
Issue-funded 323 MHE and 12 AWPs over FY27-28 (p. 88)
threats: Rental-rate competition from OEMs and other renters
Promoter group runs a same-line business (non-compete in place, p. 213)

flags: AMBER: DCF and relative diverge by -46.9% - the divergence is the finding; name its cause

AMBER: TV above 75% of EV - DCF is mostly a terminal guess
model.reverse_dcf: The price asks the business to deliver 26.1 times its current free cash flow, in perpetuity.
